findings.problem: The counted noun is fixed as the plural باریاں, but Urdu agrees a counted noun with the number that precedes it in the clause: 1 باری, 2 باریاں. The chip prints the noun straight after {completed}, so the first completed turn of any running loop reads 10 میں سے 1 باریاں (proved by real render, not by inspection). English reads correctly at every value because its noun agrees with of {total}. The English argument is a number and locale-parity pins the type, so no plural arm can be added to fix it here. Meaning is never in doubt and nothing unsafe follows, which is why this is minor rather than major.
findings.fix_note: The classifier form this same file already uses in ui.chat.checkpoint.turn and checkpoint.jump_* (باری {turn}), grammatical at every count and still carrying both numbers. If the noun must stay a count noun, {total, number} باریوں میں سے {completed, number} keeps agreement with the total instead, which is correct for the total >= 2 a running loop reaches.

observations_not_findings.topic: RTL hazard: {digits} range reverses inside the Urdu sentence
observations_not_findings.detail: ui.chat.question_dock.hint.options passes digits = 1-3 (question-dock.tsx:225-227). Rendered with real intl-messageformat and reordered by FriBidi under an RTL base direction, the line shows the range as 3-1: the hyphen is a neutral between two number runs, takes the paragraph direction, and splits the range (measured with fribidi; the shaped visual line reads ... جواب دیتا ہے 3-1 ... Enter). The catalogue text is correct and shaped like the English; the fix belongs at the call site, exactly as src/renderer/src/features/agent-hub/components/hub-skills-library.tsx:631 does it (FSI/PDI around the interpolated value, reason recorded there). Reported for the renderer lane; it does not change this catalogue verdict.

observations_not_findings.topic: RTL hazard: the pass-through {body} sentence keeps its final stop at the far left
observations_not_findings.detail: ui.chat.provider_error.headline.out_of_credits ends with {body}, the provider's own English sentence (sample: Top up to continue.). Under an RTL paragraph the final full stop is a trailing neutral that takes the paragraph direction and lands at the visual left edge, detached from the sentence (measured with fribidi). Same class and same remedy as UUR-O1; the provider sentence itself is never translated, so no catalogue wording can fix it.

observations_not_findings.topic: ASCII ellipsis in mermaid.loading mirrors the English source
observations_not_findings.detail: ui.chat.mermaid.loading is the only one of the file's five ellipsis values that uses three ASCII dots - and the English source uses three ASCII dots there too ('Loading diagram...'), while the other four are U+2026 in both files. The ur value is therefore a faithful copy, not a typography slip introduced by translation; if the programme wants one ellipsis convention it should change the English source, which will then move this key in every locale.
